example_summary: Analysis of disallowance under section 40(a)(ia) for interest, salary, and commission paid by Mr. Yuvan Raja during financial year 2025-26.
source_provision:
| Nature of Payment / Expenditure | Applicable TDS Section & Threshold Conditions | Statutory Disallowance Rule u/s 40(a)(ia) | Tax Treatment & Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Interest to Resident Firm** | **Section 194A**: Applicable only if total turnover of the individual or HUF payer in the immediately preceding previous year exceeds **₹ 100 Lakhs** (business) or **₹ 50 Lakhs** (profession). | No obligation to deduct tax at source if previous year turnover does not exceed the statutory threshold limits. | **No disallowance** under Section 40(a)(ia) as no default in TDS obligation arises.
| **Salary to Resident Individual** | **Section 192**: Mandatory for **all assessee-employers** irrespective of turnover or gross receipts limits in the preceding previous year. | Failure to deduct tax at source attracts disallowance under Section 40(a)(ia) read with Chapter XVII-B. | **30% disallowance** of the salary sum payable or paid is triggered under Section 40(a)(ia).
| **Commission to Resident** | **Section 194H** (exceeding **₹ 20,000**) and **Section 194M** (aggregate exceeding **₹ 50 Lakhs**): Applicable if previous year turnover exceeds **₹ 100 Lakhs** or threshold aggregate is breached. | If previous year turnover is below **₹ 100 Lakhs** and aggregate payment does not exceed **₹ 50 Lakhs**, no TDS liability arises. | **No disallowance** under Section 40(a)(ia) due to absence of statutory requirement to deduct tax at source.


> [!IMPORTANT] Turnover Threshold Rule:
> For individual and HUF assessees, the obligation to deduct tax at source under sections like Section 194A, Section 194H, Section 194I, Section 194J, and Section 194M is triggered only if their total sales, gross receipts, or turnover from business exceeds ₹ 100 Lakhs, or from profession exceeds ₹ 50 Lakhs, in the immediately preceding previous year.


> [!WARNING] Universal Applicability of Section 192:
> Section 192 governing tax deduction at source on salary has no turnover threshold exemption. Every employer, regardless of turnover size, must deduct tax at source from salary payments, failing which Section 40(a)(ia) 30% disallowance squarely applies.

director.justification: The question evaluates multiple independent expenditure items against different statutory threshold conditions and rules under section 40(a)(ia).
director.visual_metaphor: A tax compliance gate checking individual expenditure items against turnover thresholds and statutory provisions.

Examine the interest payment of 45,000 to Rehman & Co. under Section 194A and turnover limits.

Evaluate the commission payment of 26,000 to Mr. Vidyasagar under Section 194H and Section 194M.
Compute the final disallowance under Section 40(a)(ia) totaling 4,50,000 for salary.
Summarize the final tax treatment for all three expenditure items.
